_comment: Known-good decode configs per machine. Throughput is NOT monotonic in batch size, so these are measured, not calculated. Add yours: run `mlx-asr-bench` and open an issue with its output. Keys are matched as substrings of `sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string` plus a RAM bucket. Machines with no entry fall through to a derived formula (see hardware.py: derive_batch), not to a bucket table.

_schema.batch: rows decoded in lockstep; the single most important knob
_schema.chunk_seconds: audio per row; shorter = fewer decode steps but more seams (worse CER)
_schema.measured_x_realtime: end-to-end on the reference clip, incl. model load
_schema.peak_gb: GPU peak at this batch; keep under ~60% of gpu_working_set_gb
_schema.source: who measured it and on what

profiles.notes: 10 GPU cores, ~120GB/s. 60s chunks need no overlap (few seams); with --fast the CLI drops to 30s/B32 where overlap earns 1.8 CER points back. B=4..8 is a hard valley (110ms/step vs 22ms at B=1) and B=48 exceeds the ~8.4GB KV wall. The encoder is 36% of wall clock and compute-bound, so shorter chunks stop paying well before the batch limit.

60 GPU cores, ~800GB/s. 21.4x at CER 7.37%; --fast gives 30s/B32 + 8s overlap for 26.7x at 7.25%, which is the best speed/accuracy point measured on any machine. A whole 935s clip fits in one batch of 16, so long chunks cost nothing beyond the decode length of the longest row.

derived._comment: Inputs to hardware.py:derive_batch, used only when no profile above matches. Batch itself is computed from GPU working set, GPU cores, model weight size and chunk length, then snapped onto FAST_BATCHES; it is deliberately NOT a table, because memory and core count are detectable at runtime while the batch-size valley is not.
derived._chunk_note: 60s both ways for now. Shorter chunks trade seam accuracy for decode steps, and on a low-core GPU the compute-bound encoder makes short chunks a net loss; that is measured on the M4 but not yet on any other low-core part, so the two values are kept separate rather than collapsed.
